# Min Max Game.

@example The first squeeze gives min(7,5), max(1,3), min(8,6), max(2,9) = [5,3,6,9]; the next gives [3,9], and the last the smaller of 3 and 9.
[7,5,1,3,8,6,2,9]
=> 3

@example Pair 0 gives 10 and pair 1 gives 4, the larger of 3 and 4; then the smaller of 10 and 4 is left.
[10,20,3,4]
=> 4

@example A single value needs no squeeze.
[500]
=> 500

# Two values: pair 0 always gives the smaller, in either order.
[9,4]
=> 4

[4,9]
=> 4

# Equal values.
[5,5]
=> 5

[3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3]
=> 3

# Four values where pair 0 wins: min(6,7) = 6 against max(1,9) = 9. The
# answer is neither the smallest nor the largest value.
[6,7,1,9]
=> 6

# The bounds of the values.
[1000000000,1]
=> 1

[1000000000,1000000000,1000000000,1]
=> 1000000000

# The answer is the last value: [50,60,40,45,10,20,5,30] becomes
# [50,45,10,30], then [45,30], then 30.
[50,60,40,45,10,20,5,30]
=> 30

# Sixteen values: [22,18,27,25,8,11,9,12], then [18,27,8,12], then
# [18,12], then 12. Taking the smaller in a whole squeeze and the larger
# in the next would give 22; swapping smaller and larger would give 31.
[22,31,16,18,40,27,13,25,8,14,11,5,21,9,3,12]
=> 12
